hero.title: I build full-stack solutions with modern technology, following best practices

data.title: Data engineering
data.subtitle: I engineer scalable data platforms built around robust ingestion, orchestration, data modeling, distributed processing, and infrastructure that can handle changing schemas and growing workloads.
data.diagramAlt: Architecture of a data platform in five layers: sources, ingestion, storage (raw, curated, consumption), processing and serving, with orchestration, governance and observability & cost spanning every layer.

ai.title: AI engineering
ai.subtitle: I build production-ready AI systems with a focus on data privacy, traceability, evaluation and reliable data pipelines.
ai.diagramAlt: Architecture of an AI agent system: an input gateway with auth and input guardrails, an orchestrator agent that plans tasks and hands them to specialist agents, a tool layer (functions and MCP), memory and knowledge (vector store / RAG), output guardrails with a human in the loop and a critic loop, and observability and governance around it all.

experience.title: Where I've done this before
experience.subtitle: Two environments where a wrong figure has real consequences, and one where explaining is the whole job.

items.body: Data analysis, automation and AI within criminal law — under hard privacy and information-security requirements, where privacy by design is the starting point rather than an appendix.
Built a wide range of data projects in a research environment where the numbers are checked, and the pipelines behind them have to hold up to that.
Courses that explain complex technology to people without a technical background: 241 students with a 4.2 rating. A dashboard nobody understands isn't a dashboard — and the same goes for a handover.

principles.title: What you get when I join the team
principles.subtitle: Four habits that come back in every project on this site — and in the code behind them.
principles.card1Body: Most AI and reporting projects fail on the data, not the model. I start with the grain, the definitions and the tests — and only then with what sits on top.
principles.card2Body: At the police and in aerospace you work under hard privacy and information-security requirements. Privacy by design is how I start, not an afterthought.
principles.card3Body: Since 2020 I've explained complex technology on Udemy to people without a technical background: 241 students with a 4.2 rating. I do the same with stakeholders and teammates.
principles.card4Body: Tests, CI and documentation are part of every project — check the repos. The goal is work a team can carry on with, not work that depends on me.

digital-twin.title: An AI that speaks about me — only when it can cite me
digital-twin.sub: A digital twin for this site: a LangGraph agent over my CV, projects and writing that streams cited answers, refuses when it has no source, stays under a daily cost cap, and pauses for my approval before it acts on my behalf.
digital-twin.f1Body: Prompt-injection, PII and off-topic screens run in plain Python before a single token is spent — every guard fails closed, never crashes.
digital-twin.f2Body: Drafting a message on my behalf is high-risk: the graph interrupts, queues it for my approval, and tells the visitor it's waiting for review.
digital-twin.f3Body: Two labelled datasets against the real agent — tool selection ≥ 95%, task completion ≥ 90% — with failure injection to prove the retries hold.

open-data-warehouse.title: A star schema in the open, on data anyone can check
open-data-warehouse.sub: End-to-end ELT platform on Dutch open data: Python ingestion, dbt transformations and a documented Kimball star schema — with tests and CI on every pull request, built the way a platform team delivers it.
open-data-warehouse.f1Body: Two fact tables with different grains in one schema, each pinned down in a single sentence — because that's exactly where modelling goes wrong.
open-data-warehouse.f2Body: dbt tests and docs run on every pull request; a broken model never reaches main.
open-data-warehouse.f3Body: DuckDB in CI, Snowflake or Databricks with a profile switch — the modelling is the point, not the engine.

ov-streaming-pipeline.title: Real-time delays across Dutch public transport
ov-streaming-pipeline.sub: Streaming pipeline on the national OV feed: vehicle positions flow through Kafka, delay aggregates are computed in five-minute windows, and a live map shows where the network runs late — right now.
ov-streaming-pipeline.f1Body: GTFS-realtime vehicle positions consumed through Redpanda, with a dead-letter queue for events that don't parse.
ov-streaming-pipeline.f2Body: Delay per line and station in five-minute tumbling windows — correct under late and duplicate events.
ov-streaming-pipeline.f3Body: A Streamlit map of current delays, fed straight from the stream.

strafrecht-rag.title: Ask questions of Dutch case law — with sources
strafrecht-rag.sub: RAG system over court rulings: semantic search across judgments, answers formulated by an LLM, and every claim traced back to the ECLI it came from.
strafrecht-rag.f1Body: Every answer carries its ECLI references — from claim back to the underlying passage.
strafrecht-rag.f2Body: No relevant passage retrieved means no answer. The system doesn't improvise case law.
strafrecht-rag.f3Body: Retrieval quality is measured against a test set with LangFuse tracing — not a demo that went well once.

about.metaTitle: About me — data engineer with a background at NLR and the Dutch police
about.metaDescription: Data engineer and AI builder with 241 Udemy students at a 4.2 rating. Designed and built a data platform at the Netherlands Aerospace Centre and set up data-driven working at the Noord-Holland police. Open to new roles.
about.name: Ruud Juffermans
about.intro1: At the Noord-Holland police unit I set up data-driven working in a team that didn't have it yet. I mapped the data sources, built pipelines in Python and SQL, designed the data models and delivered the reports that detectives and managers now steer by. All of that happens under strict privacy and information-security requirements, with data where a wrong conclusion has real consequences.
about.intro2: Before that I was a data engineer at the Netherlands Aerospace Centre (NLR), working on COMPASS, an EU project on digital product passports. I led requirements engineering with partners across Europe, made the architecture decisions for the data platform and built the MVP in an international Agile team. My degree in Business Data Management laid the groundwork: data modeling, data warehousing and BI.
about.intro3: Alongside that work I spent four years creating Udemy courses on Python, SQL and full-stack development. Explaining complex technology to people without a technical background is the entire job there — and it's also what a data engineer on a team does most of the day. The same curiosity led me to AI: RAG, agents and retrieval evaluation, worked out in the projects on this site. I'm now looking for a team where I can build that data foundation and the AI layer on top of it, together.
about.pullQuote: I've seen what happens when data and AI work — and what happens when the foundation is missing.
about.experienceTitle: Roles, and what I did there

bullets: Set up data-driven working from scratch: inventoried data sources, assessed their quality and translated the needs of operations, tactics and management into a concrete plan.
Built ETL pipelines in Python and SQL, dimensional data models and Power BI reports for operational and strategic decision-making.
Developed automated tooling that replaces manual analysis work, including for financial and cryptocurrency investigations.
Put governance in place — data quality, classification, documentation — and gave training to raise data literacy in the team.
Led requirements engineering for COMPASS, an EU-funded project on digital product passports: turned interviews with European partners into specifications.
Designed the data platform architecture — integrations, data models, data structures — and built and iteratively delivered the MVP in an international Agile team.
Built data transformations with dbt and developed Power BI dashboards for project stakeholders.
Developed courses on Python, SQL, full-stack development and blockchain technology: 241 students with a 4.2 rating.
Built an education product independently: from audience analysis to iterative improvement based on student feedback.

data.metaTitle: Data engineering — warehouses, pipelines and streaming
data.metaDescription: How I approach data engineering: modelled warehouses, tested pipelines and streaming — with the experience at NLR and the Police and the projects that show it.
data.title: From scattered sources to one warehouse that adds up
data.intro: I bring sources together into a modelled, tested data warehouse: pipelines that run every day, figures that are the same for every department, and reporting nobody has to assemble by hand anymore.
data.intro2: That's the work I did as a data engineer at the Netherlands Aerospace Centre and as a data analyst at Politie Noord-Holland — two environments where a wrong figure has real consequences. The projects on this site show the same approach, with the code in the open.
data.approachTitle: What a team can expect from me

approach.title: Model before building
approach.body: Grain and dimensions on paper first, SQL second. A documented star schema stays understandable after I've moved on.

approach.title: Tests on every change
approach.body: Not-null, uniqueness and relationships as tests in the pipeline, with CI running them on every pull request. A mistake surfaces before it reaches a dashboard.

approach.title: Batch and streaming
approach.body: Daily ELT where that's enough, Kafka and windows where figures have to be right within minutes — including a dead-letter queue and replay for the failure path.

approach.title: Explainable to the business
approach.body: A warehouse isn't finished until the people using it understand it. Documentation and handover are part of the work, not an afterthought.

experience.body: Data analysis and automation within criminal law, under hard privacy and information-security requirements. Pipelines where privacy by design is the starting point, not an appendix.
A wide range of data projects in a research environment where the figures get checked — and where the pipelines behind them have to hold up to that.
Courses on data and technology for people without a technical background: 241 students with a 4.2 rating. The same skill a team needs at every handover.

principles: One definition per figure, the same for every department.
Mistakes surface in the pipeline, not in the dashboard.
Everything reproducible: from zero with one command.

ai.metaTitle: AI engineering — assistants with sources, guardrails and evaluation
ai.metaDescription: How I approach AI engineering: RAG and agents that answer with citations, refuse honestly and only act with approval — with the experience at the Police and the projects that show it.
ai.title: AI that answers with sources, and knows when to stay silent
ai.intro: I build AI systems for production: assistants that answer with citations, say honestly what they don't know, and only act where a person has approved it — with evaluation guarding every change.
ai.intro2: At Politie Noord-Holland I applied AI within criminal law, an environment where privacy and information security are not an afterthought. Most AI projects fail on the data, not the model; so I build the foundation first and the assistant second.
ai.approachTitle: What a team can expect from me

approach.title: Sources behind every claim
approach.body: An answer without a retrieved passage is no answer. Every claim points to the document or ruling it came from.

approach.title: Guardrails before the model
approach.body: Prompt injection, PII and off-topic questions are caught in plain code before a single token is spent. Fail closed, never crash.

approach.title: Human in the loop
approach.body: Actions with consequences — sending a message, changing something — wait for approval. A hard daily cost limit keeps the bill predictable.

approach.title: Evaluation on every change
approach.body: Labelled datasets and thresholds in CI: retrieval recall, correct tool selection, task completion. A regression blocks the merge.

experience.body: Applied AI and automation within criminal law — where confidential and privacy-sensitive data is the norm and every outcome has to be traceable.
Built the data foundation AI applications have to stand on: clean, modelled and tested data in a research environment.
Explaining complex technology to people without a technical background, 241 students with a 4.2 rating — including what AI can and cannot do.

principles: Guards in code, not in the prompt.
Risky actions only with human approval.

privacy.metaDescription: Privacy statement of ruudjuffermans.nl, the portfolio site of Ruud Juffermans.
privacy.title: Privacy statement

sections.title: 1. Who I am
sections.content: Ruud Juffermans, data engineer, based in Noord-Holland, Netherlands. This is my personal portfolio site. Email: ruudjuffermans@pm.me.

sections.title: 2. What data I collect
sections.content: Via the contact form: name, email address, optional company name and your message. Via the newsletter: email address. I use privacy-friendly analytics (no cookies, no personal data).

sections.title: 3. Why I collect this data
sections.content: To answer your message and contact you. To send the newsletter you signed up for. To improve the website based on anonymized usage statistics.

sections.title: 4. How long I keep data
sections.content: Contact-form data is kept as long as needed to handle your message, up to a maximum of 12 months. Newsletter data is kept until you unsubscribe.

sections.title: 5. Sharing with third parties
sections.content: I don't share your data with third parties, except where needed to run the site: Proton (email sending) and Buttondown (newsletter). These processors operate under data-processing agreements.

sections.title: 6. Your rights
sections.content: You have the right to access, correct, delete and transfer your data. You can also object to processing. Contact ruudjuffermans@pm.me for any of these. You can also file a complaint with the Dutch Data Protection Authority.

sections.title: 7. Cookies
sections.content: This website doesn't use tracking cookies. No cookie banner is needed.

sections.title: 8. Changes
sections.content: This privacy statement may be updated. The latest version is always available on this page.
